description: JIT utility-first CSS engine. Class names are generated on demand, but the vocabulary is finite and fully enumerated here.

naming.px: The px unit attaches directly: p-16px
naming.units: rem / em / vh / vw use a dash: p-1-5-rem, gap-10vh
naming.bareNumbers: A bare number is a legacy alias resolved as em, then px, then rem: p-1 is 1em, p-16 is 16px, p-2-5 is 2.5rem
naming.important: Every utility except animate-* is emitted with !important
naming.notTailwind: These are NOT Tailwind names. p-4 is valid but means 4px (not 1rem). text-sm does not exist.
naming.noColors: There are no colour utilities and no colour scale. Theme through CSS variables (e.g. --border) or your own classes.
naming.breakpoints: Append -m (mobile) or -t (tablet) to any base utility.

exceptions.reason: .border-t is itself a class, and the engine resolves the raw name before stripping the suffix

semanticTraps.p-4: a bare number in the spacing family means px (after em), not rem — so p-4 is padding: 4px. Use p-1-rem for 1rem.
semanticTraps.m-2: 2px, not 0.5rem. The legacy bare-number alias resolves as em, then px, then rem.
semanticTraps.p-1: 1em, because em wins over px and rem for bare numbers.
semanticTraps.w-50: a bare number in the sizing family is always a percentage — w-50 is width: 50%. Use w-50px or w-50vw for units.
semanticTraps.fs-1: a bare number in the font-size family is rem — fs-1 is font-size: 1rem.
semanticTraps.rounded-md: 8px here, not Tailwind's 6px. The named radius scale is xs(2) sm(4) md(8) lg(12) xl(16) 2xl(24) full(9999).
semanticTraps.lh-1-5: the dash is a decimal point, so this is line-height: 1.5.
semanticTraps.lh-4-5: only 1, 2, 3, 4 and 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5 exist — there is no lh-1-25.
semanticTraps.h-100vh: viewport height works for h and w only. min-h and max-h accept pixels, so Tailwind's min-h-screen has no equivalent here.
semanticTraps.border: paints 1px solid var(--border); set --border to theme it.
semanticTraps.animate-spin: the only family emitted without !important, so it stays overridable.

families.title: Background reset
families.summary: Clears the background or sets it to transparent.

families.title: Display
families.docs: The `-i` variant is an explicit alias kept for parity with the legacy stylesheet; it emits the same declarations.

families.title: Sizing — percentages
families.docs: A bare number is always a percentage. Use `w-100px` or `w-100vw` for other units.

families.title: Offsets
families.summary: Edge offsets in px/rem/em or anchors: `top-0`, `left-50-percent`, `top-16px`, `right-1-5-rem`.
families.docs: `start` maps to `left` and `end` maps to `right`, mirroring the logical-side helpers.

families.title: Transform helpers
families.summary: Named transform shortcuts for centring and rotating.

families.title: Vertical align
families.docs: Not to be confused with `align-items-*`, which is flexbox alignment.

families.title: Z-index
families.summary: Stacking order: `z-1`…`z-10`, decades up to `z-100`, plus presets like `z-9999`.

families.title: Spacing — margin, padding, gap
families.docs: Directions: `t` `b` `l` `r` `s` `e` (single side), `x` `y` (axis). Units: `px` has no dash (`p-16px`); `rem`, `em`, `vh`, `vw` use a dash (`p-1-5-rem`). A bare number is a legacy alias: `em` wins, then `px`, then `rem` — so `p-1` is `1em` but `p-16` is `16px`. Only the margin family accepts `auto`: `m-auto`, `mx-auto`, `mt-auto`, `mb-auto`, `ms-auto`, `me-auto`, `my-auto`.

families.title: Borders
families.docs: Borders paint `1px solid var(--border)`, so the theme variable drives the colour.

families.title: Animations
families.summary: Ready-made keyframe animations; the `@keyframes` block is emitted on demand.
families.docs: Animations are the only utilities emitted without `!important`, so they stay overridable.
